newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium takes new measures on Dutch swine fever.
newsitem.headline: Belgium takes new measures on Dutch swine fever.

text.p: Belgium on Thursday announced new measures in areas near the Dutch border to prevent highly contagious swine fever from spreading from the Netherlands where new outbreaks were reported this week.

Agriculture Minister Karel Pinxten imposed an immediate slaughter and transport ban on all husbandry animals in the towns of Ravels, Baarle-Hertog and Turnhout after swine fever was found in the Dutch towns of Baarle-Nassau and Soerendonk.
At the same time Pinxten lifted such a ban imposed seven weeks ago for the Hoogstraten area after thorough testing and the absence of any reported cases of swine fever.
Belgium banned all imports of pigs from Germany on February 1 and added a ban on imports from the Netherlands 11 days later.
Cases of swine fever were first reported in Germany at the start of the year.
Belgium has slaughtered and tested 15,142 pigs imported from the Netherlands between January 15 and February 12. All the carcasses, weighing a total of 510 tonnes, were destroyed.
